summary: @onereach/si-textinput preinstall downloads Bun runtime to execute obfuscated shipped payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue text-input UI component but ships an install-time dropper. package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs constructs a versioned URL against `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/...`, downloads the Bun runtime binary, chmods it 0755, and then invokes it via `execFileSync(bunPath, [join(D, 'math_init.js')])`. The sibling `math_init.js` is a 727 KB `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle heavily obfuscated with a shuffled string-array and rotation routine (`function WV8StW(...) {... MmgoCP.push(MmgoCP.shift()); }` plus a large `n7gIxM=[...]` constants table decoded at runtime). This file is not exposed through `main`, `module`, or the library's public entry — it exists solely to be executed at install time under an alternate runtime that Node-based tooling does not evaluate. The declared UI-component purpose is unrelated to shipping and executing a second-language runtime plus an opaque bundle, and the runner script itself is obfuscated (`_0x…` identifiers, dictionary-object indirection) to hide the flow. Installing the package causes attacker-controlled bytes to run on the installer's host at `npm install` time under a hidden interpreter.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
